 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. LeBron James was impressed by the performance from his youngest son, Bryce James, in the Arizona Wildcats' 90-59 win over Northern Arizona University on November 10. 
 James is hoping to find a way onto the Wildcats' rotation for the 2026-27 season as a red-shirt freshman who developed on the bench last season as the program went all the way to the Final Four of the NCAA Tournament.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Head coach Tommy Lloyd has shown a willingness to play and develop Bryce, which has started to bear fruit for the 19-year-old forward, as evidenced by his performance in their latest win.
 Bryce James' highlight has his father LeBron James feeling proud
 Bryce put up three points with two assists, two steals and a block against NAU in 13 minutes. His sole block was an emphatic at-rim denial which went viral, with even his father watching as an impressed fan by his well-rounded highlights from this win.
 "1% each day young (king)!"
 LeBron also reshared Bryce's block as an individual highlight in the Instagram story prior to the one with the message, showing the 41-year-old was locked in on watching his son's minutes on the same day he struggled in a 123-101 loss to the Boston Celtics.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bryce is averaging 2.7 points and 1.7 assists in his three appearances so far. While he started Arizona's season-opener against UCLA, he only played six minutes in that clash.
 The other games came against much-weaker opposition where Bryce played more minutes, but not nearly enough to indicate he will play a key role in the team's rotation for more consequential games later in the season.
 Bryce is not expected to be an offensive difference-maker for the Wildcats, with coach Lloyd likely relying on his defensive ability to provide balance on that end of the court when he plays.
 It's a long season ahead for Bryce and the Wildcats, as well as for LeBron in the NBA, but everyone involved is hoping that Bryce can fulfill his potential over multiple years in the NCAA rather than jumping to the NBA as early as possible like Bryce did.
